title: AI Gamedev Workflows
author: Qumfur
selftext:
Let's talk about the workflows for AI Gamedev. I have an idea for a game or maybe lets call it a dream. 

So far, I've been using Google Antigravity for some prototyping and trying out smaller ideas (I made a sudoku app for my girlfriend which worked really quickly and well). However for an actual game it seems to be not enough and I want to learn a better way of using it's potential. I cannot do any art in it directly and I've been using other Google environments so far for static sprites but animations feel almost impossible with this.

So, what are you using? Which programs are you using for different tasks? What subscriptions are you using? How fast are you reaching the token limits? Do you write skills to assist your workflow? How does the AI keep track of the codebase without needing enormous amounts of input tokens? Do you know any good videos/blogs/etc. where I can read up on it?

comments.author: Blake9712
comments.body: Rn I’m only using Claude. My game is just a 2D rogue like and I do use all of my $20 plan tokens pretty fast and have for the past 6 months when I started. For my workflow, my game lives within an asset builder so I just build,  test and request bug fixes then features. I really don’t do anything special but I’ve let Claude write a very large MD so even if I go to a new chat it doesn’t have trouble keeping track of my code base (which is somewhere around 30k lines for the asset builder, I haven’t looked at my assets in terms of size if that’s relevant) I’ve tried gpt but it drained a weeks worth of tokens with very little output. This was before Astra came out. It has taken me about 6 months so far at about an hour average a day without much progress and filming every usage limit tho. I just built an asset builder for my game and whenever I ask Claude to make assets it knows to do it within the bounds of the builder and with the same style I use. Honestly you can make anything with enough time and care but it takes a ton of time.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: I think there’s probably something you could do to make the agents much more efficient and actually get significant work done. Long-running chats and very large markdown files can cause problems, and may explain why you’re draining tokens.

replies.author: Blake9712
replies.body: I do have large mark down files and I fill up context pretty fast. I don’t have long running chats but I’ll hit 40-50% context in a prompt or two some times. You’re probably right and I wonder if there’s something else, like is cause reading all 30k lines of code every prompt?  Or is it really just the MD? Everything goes real real real bad when Claude doesn’t read the MD so I have never once messed with it.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body:
1M context window? 40-50% means 400k-500k tokens, which is very large. You’re definitely seeing context rot.

Ask Claude this question:

> What symptoms of context rot should I expect when I hit 40-50% of Claude’s context window?

I am finishing most work around 100k.

Claude shouldn’t be reading all 30k lines of code. Have your code organized into modules and add a docs that explain what each module does. The idea is to make it so that when you’re working on a module, the LLM only has to read that particular module, maybe some others.
